examples.problem_statement: What is the minimum possible perimeter of a quadrilateral with an area of 1,600 square feet?

solution.operation: \text{minimize } P \text{ for fixed } A \Rightarrow \text{quadrilateral is a square}
solution.description: Start by fixing the shape: among all quadrilaterals of a given area, the square is the one with the smallest perimeter, so treat the figure as a square.
Use the square's area formula, side length squared, set it equal to 1,600 square feet, and take the square root to get the side length.
Multiply that side length by four, since a square's perimeter is four times its side, to get the minimum perimeter.

key_reminders: For a fixed area, the quadrilateral of minimum perimeter is a square.
Area of a square is s^2, so s = \sqrt{A}.
common_mistakes: Solving for a maximum perimeter instead: with non-integer sides there is no maximum, since 1600 \times 1, 3200 \times 0.5, and so on give ever-longer perimeters as the shape flattens toward a line.
Reporting the side length 40 instead of the perimeter 160.

concept.technique_name: percent change on a shifting base

examples.problem_statement:
From 2003 to 2004, the rent on a certain property increased by x%. From 2004 to 2005, the rent then decreased by x%. x is a positive integer.
Quantity A: The difference between 2004's rent and 2003's rent, in dollars.
Quantity B: The difference between 2004's rent and 2005's rent, in dollars.
(A) Quantity A is greater. (B) Quantity B is greater. (C) The two quantities are equal. (D) The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.result: 2004's rent is the larger of the two bases
solution.description: Notice that the actual rent is unknown, but because 2003 to 2004 was an increase, 2004's rent must be higher than 2003's - that comparison of the two bases is the whole question.

solution.result: Quantity A is x percent of 2003's price
solution.description: Express the first dollar change: the rise from 2003 to 2004 is x percent taken of 2003's price.

solution.result: Quantity B is x percent of 2004's price
solution.description: Express the second dollar change: the fall from 2004 to 2005 is the same x percent, but taken of 2004's price.
Compare the two expressions: the same percent applied to a larger whole gives a larger dollar amount, so the second change beats the first.
Confirm with numbers by picking a rent of $100 and x = 10, which gives $110 in 2004 and $99 in 2005; the $11 drop is bigger than the $10 rise.

key_reminders: A percent change is always taken of the value it starts from, so the base matters as much as the rate.
An x% increase followed by an x% decrease does not return to the original value.
Picking a base of 100 is a fast way to verify a percent comparison.
common_mistakes: Assuming the up-x% and down-x% changes cancel and choosing (C) because the rate x is identical in both years.
Choosing (D) because the actual 2003 rent is never given, when the direction of the comparison is fixed regardless of that rent.

concept.technique_name: inference from passage detail with choice elimination

examples.problem_statement:
Select one answer choice. Based on the accompanying reading passage about male nightingales' song rate: The passage implies that during the day before a night on which a male nightingale's song rate is high, that nightingale probably does which of the following?
A. Expends less of its reserves on thermoregulation than on other days
B. Stores more energy as body reserves than on other days
C. Hides to avoid predators

solution.operation: test A against the thermoregulation reference in line 24
solution.description: Check choice A by locating the passage's only mention of thermoregulation, at line 24, and note that it describes nighttime activity rather than what the bird does during the day.

solution.operation: test B against the second paragraph on fat deposits and body mass at dusk
solution.description: Check choice B against the second paragraph, which says birds store energy as fat deposits estimable from body mass and that body mass at dusk was significantly higher before high-song-rate nights - that higher dusk mass means more was stored during the day.

solution.operation: test C against the predator reference in line 3 and the foraging reference in line 20
solution.description: Check choice C: the passage says singing exposes birds to predators at line 3 but never suggests any special hiding effort, and line 20 says nightingales spend extra time foraging, which is the opposite of hiding.

solution.operation: select the only choice with passage support
solution.description: With A and C eliminated on textual grounds, select B as the one implication the passage actually supports.

examples.answer: Choice B: Stores more energy as body reserves than on other days

key_reminders: An inference must be traceable to specific lines of the passage, not to plausible outside reasoning.
Match the time frame the question asks about - here daytime behavior, not nighttime.
A detail the passage mentions is not automatically an answer unless it supports the claim in the choice.
common_mistakes: Picking A because thermoregulation is genuinely discussed, without checking that the discussion is about the night rather than the preceding day.
Picking C by extending the passage's predator remark into a hiding behavior the passage never states, while it in fact reports extra foraging.
